title: Call on them. They cannot lift your hardship, or even shift it.
subtitle: Testing what you rely on
then: The Prophet ﷺ was told to challenge the idolaters directly: go ahead and call on them. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they have no power at all{/trap} to remove a hardship, or even to pass it onto someone else. {idea}Only Allah can do that{/idea}, the One who creates and commands.
now: The test results come back bad. You refresh the forum, call the specialist, read every article at 2am. All of that is fine. {idea}But none of it can lift this.{/idea} Make sure your first and last call is to Him.
old: The right expert or connection can fix my problem.
new: People are means, but only Allah can remove or even shift a hardship.
try: Before your next appointment or call about a problem, make dua for it first.

title: The ones they worship are themselves racing to get closer to Allah.
subtitle: Hope and fear, the two wings of worship
then: Ibn 'Abbas said the idolaters worshipped angels and others who {idea}were themselves calling on Allah{/idea}. Ibn Mas'ud reported that some jinn who were worshipped later became Muslims. Ibn Kathir adds that {reward}worship is complete only with fear and hope together{/reward}: fear holds you back from sin, hope moves you to do good.
now: Some days you feel so sure of Allah's mercy you get careless. Other days you feel so afraid you give up. {idea}Both are a wing missing.{/idea} The righteous ones you admire most fly with both.
old: Either Allah forgives everything, or I am too far gone.
new: I hope for His mercy and fear His punishment, and that balance keeps me going.
try: Make one dua for mercy and one for protection from punishment after your next prayer.

title: Every wrongdoing town's end is already written.
subtitle: Nothing is outside His record
then: Ibn Kathir explains that it is written in the Preserved Tablet that towns will meet ruin or hardship before the Day of Resurrection {trap}because of their sins{/trap}. He cites the verse about past nations: {idea}We did not wrong them, they wronged themselves{/idea}.
now: Nothing in this world is permanent, not your city, not your company, not your street. {idea}What lasts is what you did in it.{/idea} When you see a place decline, ask what you are building in your own corner.
old: The places and systems around me will always be there.
new: Every place has a written end, so I should invest in what lasts.
try: Do one good deed today for your neighborhood, something small that helps someone nearby.

title: Signs on demand were held back, out of mercy.
subtitle: Why the miracle they asked for did not come
then: Quraysh asked the Prophet ﷺ to turn the hill of As-Safa into gold. Ibn 'Abbas narrated that Allah gave him a choice: the sign, with punishment if they still disbelieved, or {reward}the gates of repentance and mercy{/reward}. He chose mercy. The earlier peoples, like Thamud with the she-camel, {trap}had denied their signs and been destroyed{/trap}.
now: You tell yourself: if Allah just showed me something clear, I would change. But plenty of people saw and did not. {reward}The time you have right now is the mercy.{/reward} An eclipse, a tremor, a scare at the doctor are reminders too.
old: If I got a clear sign, I would finally get serious.
new: The extra time I have been given is itself a mercy and a sign.
try: Next time something frightens you, a storm or bad news, stop and make istighfar.

title: The Night Journey vision and the tree of Zaqqum were tests.
subtitle: What sorted the believers from the doubters

key.label: When it is hard to grasp

then: Ibn 'Abbas said the vision was {idea}what the Prophet ﷺ saw with his own eyes on the Night Journey{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes some people left Islam because their minds could not grasp it, while {reward}it strengthened the faith of others{/reward}. Abu Jahl mocked the tree of Zaqqum by eating dates and butter. And Allah had told the Prophet ﷺ He had encompassed the people, meaning He would protect him.
now: You hit a part of the faith that your mind struggles with. The unseen. Something that does not fit your science class. {idea}That moment is a test.{/idea} Some people walk away. Others sit with it and find their trust deepens.
old: If I cannot fully understand something in my faith, I should doubt it.
new: What my mind cannot fully grasp can still be true, and trusting it is a test.
try: Write down one thing in faith that puzzles you. Ask a teacher, and ask Allah for understanding.

title: All bowed to Adam except Iblis, who scorned the clay.
subtitle: The oldest arrogance
then: Ibn Kathir calls this {trap}an ancient hatred{/trap}, from the moment Adam was created. Iblis refused out of arrogance and said, with contempt, shall I bow to one made of clay? In another verse he says {trap}I am better than him{/trap}.
now: You look at someone and decide in a second you are better: your degree, your family, your accent, your neighborhood. {trap}That I am better than him is the first sin ever recorded against a human.{/trap}
old: Some people are simply beneath me because of where they come from.
new: Thinking I am better by birth is the voice of Iblis, not of faith.
try: Today, go out of your way to show respect to someone you tend to look down on.

title: Give me time, said Iblis, and I will mislead his children.
subtitle: The enemy's stated plan
then: Iblis spoke to his Lord with insolence, and {reward}the Lord bore it patiently{/reward}. Ibn 'Abbas said he meant: I will dominate his offspring. Mujahid said: I will surround them. Ibn Zayd: {trap}I will lead them astray, all but a few{/trap}.
now: Your enemy told everyone his plan in advance. Surround you. Wear you down. Keep you scrolling, delaying, doubting. {idea}Knowing the plan is half the defense.{/idea} Aim to be in the few.
old: I am not really a target, I am just an ordinary person.
new: Shaytan has openly declared his plan against me, so I stay alert.
try: Say a'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim the next time you feel the pull to delay a prayer.

title: Go, then. Whoever follows you shares your end.
subtitle: The respite and the warning
then: Allah granted Iblis respite until the appointed Day, and warned him and {trap}whoever of Adam's children follows him{/trap}. Qatadah said the recompense will be abundant and not decreased. The key word is follows.
now: Shaytan can whisper, but he cannot drag. Every time you open that app, scroll that feed, or say that word, {idea}you are the one taking the step{/idea}. The good news: you can also stop following.
old: When I give in to temptation, it is the devil's fault.
new: He only invites, and following him is my choice to make or refuse.
try: Identify one whisper you followed this week. Decide today to refuse it next time.

title: His voice, his forces, his share, his promises: all deceit.
subtitle: Shaytan's toolkit
then: Ibn 'Abbas said his voice is {trap}every caller who calls people to disobey Allah{/trap}. His share in wealth is money spent in disobedience. Ibn Kathir says {idea}anything in which a person obeys Shaytan, he is sharing in it{/idea}. On the Day, Iblis himself will admit: I promised you, but I betrayed you.
now: The ad that says you deserve it. The friend who says just this once. The voice that says you will repent later. {trap}A promise of later is one of his favorites.{/trap} Notice how many of his promises are about tomorrow.
old: I will enjoy this now and fix things later.
new: Shaytan's promises always break, especially the one about later.
try: Say bismillah before you spend money today, and see if it changes what you buy.

title: Over My servants you have no authority.
subtitle: The protection of being Allah's servant
then: After listing Shaytan's whole toolkit, the passage ends with reassurance. Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah supports His believing servants and guards them{/reward} against the accursed one. He is enough as a Protector, Supporter and Helper.
now: After a bad week of slipping, it can feel like the whispers always win. {reward}They do not get the last word.{/reward} The closer you hold to being His servant, prayer, dhikr, honest repentance, the less grip they have.
old: Shaytan is too strong, I will always lose to him.
new: As Allah's servant, I am under His guard, and Shaytan cannot own me.
try: Read Ayat al-Kursi before you sleep tonight and rest in His protection.

title: Your Lord drives the ship so you can seek His bounty.
subtitle: Mercy in ordinary travel and trade
then: After the warnings about Shaytan, the surah turns to Allah's kindness. Ibn Kathir says He made ships {idea}easy to use for trade between one region and another{/idea}. He does this {reward}out of His grace and mercy{/reward}.
now: The cargo ship that brought your phone. The bus you take to work. The delivery van with your groceries. {reward}A whole chain of travel brings your daily bread.{/reward} Every trip you take for your living is held up by His mercy.
old: Getting to work and earning a living is just logistics.
new: Every journey that brings me provision is a mercy from my Lord.
try: Say the travel dua, subhanalladhi sakhkhara lana hadha, on your next commute.

title: In the storm, only He remains. On land, you forget.
subtitle: Sincere in danger, careless in safety
then: 'Ikrimah bin Abi Jahl fled Makkah after its conquest and took a boat toward Ethiopia. A storm hit and the sailors said only Allah can save you. He thought: {idea}if only Allah helps at sea, only Allah helps on land{/idea}. He promised to go to the Prophet ﷺ if he survived, and he did, {reward}and became a good Muslim{/reward}.
now: The turbulence on the flight. The night in the hospital corridor. You prayed like never before. Then it passed, and within a week you were back to skipping Fajr. {idea}Be like 'Ikrimah: keep the promise you made in the storm.{/idea}
old: I turn to Allah seriously when things get really bad.
new: The Allah I called in the storm is the same Allah on calm days.
try: Remember one promise you made to Allah in a hard moment. Keep part of it today.

title: Is dry land really safer?
subtitle: The false feeling of security
then: This speaks to the person who turned away once the boat reached land. Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}do you think dry land makes you safe from Him?{/trap} Mujahid said Hasib is rain that carries stones, like what came on the people of Lut, except his family, whom {reward}Allah saved before dawn{/reward}.
now: The scare is over, the scan was clear, the job is safe. You exhale and go back to normal. {idea}Your safety today is as much a gift as your rescue was.{/idea} It is not a reason to forget Him.
old: Once the danger has passed, I am safe on my own.
new: I am never safe by myself. Every calm day is held up by Allah.
try: On a normal, calm day this week, thank Allah for one danger you are not in.

title: Or He could send you back to sea a second time.
subtitle: The storm you survived can return

row.title: no avenger
sub: no one to take your side

then: Ibn Kathir explains this is addressed to those who {trap}turn away after acknowledging Allah's Oneness at sea{/trap}. Ibn 'Abbas said the Qasif is the sea wind that breaks vessels. And {trap}no one will come to avenge them{/trap} against Allah.
now: You got through the layoff, the illness, the family crisis. Life can bring the same storm back. {idea}The rescue was not a pass.{/idea} It was a chance to come back to Him for good, while the weather is calm.
old: I already went through my hard times, so I am done with that.
new: Being rescued is a second chance, and the wise use it before the next storm.
try: Write down one way you changed after a hard time. Check that you are still doing it.
